description: READ BACK A LINE OF REASONING, read-only: an argument for and against, an experiment's case, a paper's chain of claims, a legal case. Each claim comes with its COMPUTED truth (holds, conditional, fails or unknown), the steps that support it (rule, warrant, who confirmed them), the objections against it and how each stands (`refutes`, `stands`, `answered`), its cited sources, and the routes tried toward it that fail (`failed_routes`: what was tried, the step where it fails and why — the space ruled out, which moves no reading). Then: what the reasoning rests on and which premises cite no source, the points still contested, the disputes a Decision set to `contested` keeps open on purpose, and every claim with no support. `claim` reads under one claim; omitted, every claim, refuted ones included. `map: true` reads A PROOF SEARCH AS ONE PAGE instead: the target, the holes under the claims they serve with their routes (open, failed, waiting), each closed result in one line, the rounds since progress toward the target and the branches to go back to — one reply at any size, arguments fetched by id. `what_this_means`: structure is not truth. Shown here, never raised as a gap. Bounded by `budget_chars`: every claim comes back whole, and a long proof pages with `next_offset`. Writes nothing. Ask for this to check an argument point by point: what backs each claim, what is disputed, and what has no evidence behind it.

budget_chars.description:
Characters the reply may spend (default 30,000). Over it, the page
returns FEWER claims, each WHOLE, never every claim with its words cut:
`next_offset` reads on, and `page` names the budget it was held to.

claim.description:
The claim to read the reasoning under: its support, what it rests on
and what stands against it, all the way down. Omitted: the whole
design, from every top conclusion (a node a step concludes that
supports nothing further) and every Decision set to `contested`, and
reaching every claim of the reasoning: each concluded node, each
statement, and both ends of each objection, so a refuted conjecture is
read too.

limit.description:
How many claims one page returns at most (default 60, at most 500).
The walk itself always reads the whole reasoning, up to 500 records,
so the summary lists are never one page's; `capped: true` means the
WALK stopped there, and `not_walked` names what it did not read.

map.description:
THE MAP OF A PROOF SEARCH instead of the claim-by-claim read
(req:a-proof-round-starts-from-a-one-page-map-of-its-search): with
`claim` the target, one reply at any size holding the target and how
it reads, the holes under the claims they serve (each with its routes:
open with its refuter, failed in one line, waiting with why), each
closed result in one line, the rounds since the last progress that
served the target, and the forks that hold an untried branch, highest
first. The arguments are not in it: they are fetched by id. `claim`
left out: the one search the design holds, or the targets to choose
from. `limit` and `offset` do not apply; `budget_chars` does.

offset.description:
Where in the walk the page starts (default 0, the roots): pass the
reply's `next_offset` to read on. The walk's order is proof order,
breadth first from the claim asked about.

name: reasoning_report
title: Reasoning Report
